system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: The reported time overlaps a stated collection outage for WS-MLOPEZ-01 winsec and Sysmon telemetry from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, so those sources cannot show whether PowerShell ran at about 13:40.
At 13:40:15 UTC, the proxy recorded WS-MLOPEZ-01 tunneling to download.windowsupdate.com with a Windows Update Agent user agent; the tunnel transferred about 38.8 MB from server to client.

The Windows Update connection is consistent with the organization's stated business-hours workstation patching, but does not establish that PowerShell was involved or that the reported window was benign.
At 14:17 UTC, WS-MLOPEZ-01 made an SMB connection to FILE-HD-01, and FILE-HD-01 logged the network logon as ANONYMOUS LOGON using NTLM.
The available SMB records do not identify the share or files accessed, or establish whether the connection resulted in successful access to data.
Before the stated outage, WS-MLOPEZ-01 generated a Defender scan process event, and a registry event recorded the Sysmon Operational channel as enabled.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied collection-status information says winsec and Sysmon were not collected on WS-MLOPEZ-01 from 13:30 through 14:10 UTC due to a log collection outage. This includes the reported PowerShell-window time.
Proxy and Zeek connection telemetry is available for the window, but the provided records do not expose the workstation's process tree or PowerShell command content for the reported time.
The available SMB connection and logon records do not include share-level or file-access details for the 14:17 connection.
claims_not_established: Whether PowerShell actually ran on WS-MLOPEZ-01 around 13:40 UTC, and, if so, its command line, script contents, parent process, user context, or purpose.
Whether the Windows Update tunnel was initiated by an approved patching action or by another process.
Whether the 14:17 SMB connection to FILE-HD-01 accessed a share or file, and what initiated it.
Whether any malicious activity occurred during the endpoint telemetry outage.
additional_evidence_needed: Restore or retrieve WS-MLOPEZ-01 endpoint telemetry for 13:30–14:10 UTC from alternate sources, including EDR, process-creation records, PowerShell operational logs, and script-block or transcription logs.
Review WS-MLOPEZ-01 PowerShell history and execution artifacts, such as Prefetch and relevant file or script artifacts, for the reported time.
Check patch-management records and Windows Update client logs to verify the update activity and its initiating process.
Review FILE-HD-01 SMB share and file-access auditing around 14:17 UTC to identify any requested shares or accessed files and determine the context of the anonymous logon.
